title: UK retail sales, Great Britain — November 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the Black Friday print, and it is a like-for-like one
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/retailsalesgreatbritainnovember2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200, 42,021 bytes) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Retail sales, Great Britain: November 2026', 'Release date: 18 December 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', summary 'A first estimate of retail sales in volume and value terms, seasonally and non-seasonally adjusted'. Cadence corroborated from the publisher's own bulletin index (api.beta.ons.gov.uk search, content_type=bulletin, fetched direct 2026-09-10, HTTP 200): 137 retail-sales bulletins are indexed and the eleven November-edition bulletins printed 2015-12-17 through 2025-12-19, a 14-22 December band containing 2026-12-18. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has CENSUS: for the US retail print and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-10, superseding proposals/uk-retail-sales-2026-12-18.from-uk-public-sector-finances-2026-12-22.json, read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. The proposer's DATE and its series-gap argument stand and are re-verified from the publisher. ITS TWO ANALYTICAL PREMISES DO NOT, AND BOTH REVERSE. FIRST: 'the single noisiest month for seasonal adjustment in the series' is measurably false — over 2010-2025 ex-covid the seasonally adjusted volume m/m (ONS J5EC, all retailers inc fuel) has a November standard deviation of 0.75pp, TENTH of twelve months, against January 1.62, May 1.36 and December 1.33. SECOND: the quad-witching coincidence is not a hazard, it is the modal configuration — the November-edition ONS release landed on a US quad-witching Friday in FIVE of the last SIX years (2020-12-18, 2021-12-17, 2022-12-16, 2024-12-20, 2025-12-19; only 2023 missed), and on those five dates the S&P 500's overnight gap was -0.00/-0.35/-0.12/-0.43/+0.26%, a median absolute 0.264% against 0.213% across all 2,698 sessions since 2015. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDS: the ONS RSI reporting-period rule, derived and verified. RSI months are 4-4-5 week periods ending on the Saturday nearest 31 December, so Black Friday is either the second-to-last day of the November period (+1 day) or six days after it ends -- never in between. The rule reproduces both published period strings verbatim (Nov-2019 '27 October to 23 November', Nov-2025 '2 November to 29 November') and all seven published in/out statements 2018-2025. For 2026 it gives a November period of 1-28 November with Black Friday on 27 November INSIDE it, capturing exactly the Friday and the Saturday and never Cyber Monday -- the identical configuration to the 2025 base year. So this print is unusually COMPARABLE, not unusually noisy. Tiered LOW and symbols [] because this repo tracks no UK-listed name and no house playbook is consumer-, sterling- or rates-keyed; the tier is a statement about this book's instruments, not about the print's importance to a UK-facing one. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this. Ledger: docs/research/events/uk-retail-sales-2026-12-18.md
